text:
sam: Heads-up: planning a rolling reboot + node drain in apac-edge pool to swap NIC firmware. Target window: 2024-07-18 01:00-04:00 UTC (low traffic). Will do cohorted drains (10 nodes at a time), 15m soak between cohorts. Please shout if this collides with runbooks or active experiments.

anya: noted. which pool exactly? apac-edge has two cohorts (edge-1 / edge-2) — we should avoid draining both at same time.

sam: edge-1 first, edge-2 held as backfill. We'll keep burst capacity in us-east1 as fallback for long-running batches.

leo: are we confident about cross-region routing for dedicated tenants? last time some dedicated jobs didn't failover cleanly. need a short playbook for ops team.

maria: +1 on the playbook. also can we pre-warm prefix cache after each cohort? that cut p50 by ~40ms last month.

sam: yes, plan includes prefix cache warmup: run `scripts/warm_prefix_cache --pool edge-1 --concurrency 6` after each cohort.

kevin: cost note: if we shift heavy inference into us-east for the 3h window, egress costs spike for customers with region pins. estimate ~ $1.2k extra for the window if 60% of traffic follows. want to confirm ok with finance.

anya: can we instead do staggered canaries within the region to reduce cross-region tails? e.g., drain 2 nodes, spin up canary VMs with warmed image, route 5% traffic -> canary for 30m, then ramp.

sam: yes, canary plan: 2-node canary cohort, 30m soak w/ traffic shift 5->50%. fallback uses model-variant routing to smaller quantized instance (vq-1) if latency spikes.

leo: operational checklist for each cohort:
```
- cordon nodes
- drain pods with `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120`
- verify no long-lived streaming sessions on drained nodes (check `stream-session-count` metric)
- firmware update
- reboot
- run healthcheck script `infra/check_node_health.sh <node>`
- uncordon
- warm caches
```

infra-bot: Scheduled: maintenance window created in calendar: https://calendar.internal/redwood/apac-nic-fw-2024-07-18. Pager duty rotations linked. Reminder set 30m before start.

maria: quick question — for streaming users, we should mark the route as degraded in Console so Product teams can toggle fallback to hosted smaller models. otherwise they'll see unexplained latency.

sam: good call. i'll update the rollout doc and add a Console warning line.

kevin: finance ok with up to $1.5k contingency for this window; if we exceed that we pause cross-region routing and fall back to canaries.

anya: can we run a dry-run tomorrow in the staging apac pool? low risk, same firmware behavior. 

sam: scheduled dry-run at 2024-07-17 23:00 UTC. leo, can you own verification and post a short results summary?

leo: yep. i'll check streaming metrics, kv-cache hitrate, and rerun the tail-latency eval. will post results in this thread.

maria: small nit: include `--eviction-priority=low` on the drain command so best-effort pods move before preemptible tasks.

sam: updated checklist. final plan link: https://docs.internal/ops/apac-nic-fw-rollout (will ping again with the canary IPs). :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Note: automated rollback will trigger if node reboots exceed 3 failed cohorts or avg p99 latency > 2s for >10m.

leo: FYI, discovered one tenant in apac-edge pinned to hostnames that don't resolve cross-region. i'll add a step to notify owners and exclude their nodes from auto-drain by tag.

sam: excellent — list owners here and i'll send comms.

kevin: tagging finance/ops: please approve the contingency and confirm any contractual limits for region failover.

maria: approving from SRE side.

anya: approving scheduling from infra.

sam: thanks all. will post the dry-run outcome and the final cohort roster later today.
